title: Scotch Game: the ideas
line: White opens the center at once and gets free play for its pieces.

steps.text: In the Scotch Game, White does not wait to open the center: the pawn in front of the queen goes forward early.
Push the pawn in front of your king two squares. It takes space in the center and frees your queen and a bishop.

also.d2d4: Pushing the queen's pawn is also sound and leads to other openings. This lesson pushes the king's pawn.

steps.text: Bring the knight out to attack Black's pawn on e5.

also.b1c3: That is the Vienna Game, also sound. This lesson brings this knight out.
also.f1c4: That is the Bishop's Opening, also sound. This lesson brings the knight out first.

steps.text: Push the pawn in front of your queen two squares. It attacks the pawn on e5 at once.

also.f1b5: That is the Ruy Lopez, also sound. This lesson pushes the pawn.
also.f1c4: That is the Italian Game, also sound. This lesson pushes the pawn.
also.b1c3: That leads to the Four Knights Game, also sound. This lesson pushes the pawn.

steps.text: Take back with the knight. Your pawn on e4 now stands in the center with no black pawn facing it.

also.f1c4: That is the Scotch Gambit, a lesson of its own. This lesson takes the pawn back.

steps.after: This is the Scotch Game. Here Black trades knights, as club players often do. Masters bring out a piece instead.

steps.text: Take back with the queen. She stands strong in the center, and the knight that could have chased her from c6 is gone.
steps.after: Black's knight attacks your pawn on e4. That is a slip: it lets your pawn chase the knight.

steps.text: Push the pawn on e4 one square. It chases the knight, which cannot go to d5 because your queen guards it.
steps.after: The knight goes back home; on the edge it would soon be trapped. Your pieces get free squares while Black loses time.

summary: White opens the center early, and the pieces get free squares. Black must not let a center pawn chase its pieces.
